company: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

models.long_text: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Q4_K_M GGUF, Apache-2.0) via llama.cpp llama-server

risks: 62% of revenue comes from Microsoft, exposing CoreWeave to customer concentration risk.
CoreWeave faces significant cybersecurity risks that could impact its operations and financial condition.
CoreWeave's business is reliant on third-party data centers that are vulnerable to various disruptions and cybersecurity attacks.
CoreWeave entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Weights & Biases in February 2025.
CoreWeave faces potential adverse tax impacts due to recent legislation and international tax reforms.

growth_drivers: Revenue grew from $16 million in 2022 to $1.9 billion in 2024, showing strong demand.
CoreWeave has one of the world's largest next generation GPU fleets, including NVIDIA H100, H200, and GH200.
Three of our top five committed contract customers signed agreements for additional capacity within 12 months, representing a cumulative increase of approximately $7.8 billion in committed spend.
Net cash provided by operating activities increased from $1 million in 2022 to $2.7 billion in 2024.
Revenue increased each quarter due to expanded customer demand and the ability to scale operations.
risks: The company has generated significant losses and negative cash flows, and it anticipates making significant investments in the future.
General and administrative expenses more than tripled, significantly impacting margins.
The company experienced a significant increase in loss on fair value adjustments and interest expense, impacting margins and costs.
A 100-basis point increase in interest rates would increase interest expense by approximately $31 million.
CoreWeave identified material weaknesses in its internal controls over financial reporting.

growth_drivers: Revenue increased by $1.4 billion, or 112%, in the three months ended June 30, 2026, due to increased demand from both existing and new customers.
CoreWeave provides developer tools and integrations for building and deploying models and agents, enhancing iteration from prototype to production.
risks: The company expects to continue incurring additional expenses due to projected future growth, including international expansion and compliance costs.

growth_drivers: CoreWeave delivers a comprehensive, tightly integrated platform of advanced infrastructure and proprietary software for AI systems.
Revenue increased by $3.2 billion, or 168%, due to higher demand from both existing and new customers.
As of December 31, 2025, CoreWeave had $60.7 billion of remaining performance obligations, up 302% from $15.1 billion in 2024.
CoreWeave spent $10.3 billion on capital investments in its infrastructure in 2025, up from $8.7 billion in 2024.
We plan to maintain our prioritization of investments in our engineering and product teams to continue to extend our technology leadership in AI infrastructure.
risks: Interest expense increased significantly due to higher borrowing levels, impacting cash flow.
General and administrative expenses increased significantly due to headcount growth and professional services to support expanding operations.

growth_drivers: Caterpillar is deploying NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform to support physical AI training and inference at industrial scale.
CoreWeave surpassed 1 billion model training runs tracked on its platform, indicating strong adoption and growth.
CoreWeave expects demand to meaningfully exceed supply for years, driving growth.
Q2 was an exceptional quarter marked by intense customer demand and significant ramp of active capacity.
CoreWeave expects 2026 CapEx in the range of $35 billion to $39 billion and raised its expected end of year annualized run rate revenue to $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion.
risks: CoreWeave raised approximately $18 billion in Q2, reducing its weighted average cost of debt by almost 300 basis points.

growth_drivers: CoreWeave's managed inference grew from $1 million to $100 million in a quarter.
The company can now offer compute on 2 or 3 year contracts, opening up new markets.
CoreWeave can sell GPUs from 2020 in contracts until 2029, indicating strong demand for older infrastructure.
CoreWeave expects managed inference to reach $250 million of ARR by the end of the year.
risks: CoreWeave's growth depends on maintaining high margins, which could be threatened by changes in the price environment.
